app.word: Manage custom IPS template code (allows server-side PHP execution)
Leave empty to allow every group. Primary and secondary groups are considered. The Pages block must also allow the member to view it.
Leave empty for every front-end application. This filter uses the application of the requested page, which can differ from the application that owns a shared template.
Select a block, not its containing folder. The block keeps its existing Pages permissions.

Enter the block key or a Pages tag such as {block="my_new_block"}. First create a block with this key, or replace it with the actual key of an existing block. The application resolves it to an existing block; it does not evaluate other template code.

Choose an existing Pages block or custom IPS template code, then set its placement and audience. Test a disabled rule in diagnostics before enabling it. Existing block content and permissions remain in Pages → Blocks.
Current administrator can view the block

These checks do not render content or execute its PHP expressions or advertising scripts in the ACP. Template code is compiled and checked for syntax only. The Pages permission result concerns your current administrator account. Open an actual front-end URL below to inspect matching hooks or selector counts; test the intended member groups and platforms separately. CSS placement cannot make legacy document.write tags or every third-party widget work after page load.
Native hook and HTML context available

These checks do not render the block or execute advertising scripts in the ACP. The permission result concerns your current administrator account. Open an actual front-end URL below to inspect matching hooks or selector counts; test the intended member groups and platforms separately. Prepared HTML advertising blocks are supported; CSS placement cannot make legacy document.write tags or every third-party widget work after page load.
IPS template code compiles without executing it
Enter a full URL on this community. Use the page on which you expect this rule to appear. Diagnostics on the front end are available only to administrators permitted to manage placements.
The copy was created disabled. Review its placement before enabling it.
Switch off to stop all placements without deleting their rules.
Enter an existing block key or a valid {block="my_new_block"} reference.
The configuration could not be saved. Check the content source and placement fields.
Enter a URL within this community using its configured scheme, host, and base path.
Select an available native front-end hook.
This hook position cannot safely contain a block. Choose another hook.
This placement rule no longer exists.
Enter an occurrence number of at least 1.
Choose a supported position that is valid for this target’s HTML context.
The configuration could not be saved. Check the block reference and placement fields.
Enter a nonempty CSS selector without null characters.
The CSS selector is invalid. Check its syntax before saving.
The CSS selector must be at most 1,000 characters long.
The IPS template code could not be compiled. Check its template and expression syntax.
Use native IPS template syntax rather than PHP opening or closing tags.
The IPS template code must be at most 65,535 bytes long.
URL patterns must begin with a single /, contain no domain or #fragment, and be at most 2,000 characters long.
Leave empty to exclude nobody. Any matching excluded primary or secondary group takes precedence over the allowed groups.
Use the same format as included URLs. Empty excludes nothing. Excluded patterns take precedence.
Content remains in Pages → Blocks. This form controls where an existing block appears. Test a disabled rule in diagnostics, then enable it when its placement is ready.
Available hooks come from enabled front-end templates. Positions whose HTML context cannot accept a block are omitted.
Choose an application, then a template and a hook from the current catalog of enabled front-end templates. Hooks in unsupported HTML contexts, including head and title, are not offered.

One community-relative pattern per line, beginning with /, for example /forums/*. Empty means all URLs. * is the only wildcard. The path and query are matched together; use /forums/example/* to allow varying pagination queries. Do not include the domain or a #fragment.
Each rule uses one placement mode. Native hooks render on the server. CSS rules insert the rendered block after the matching element is present in the browser.
Native hooks count render calls within each request. CSS selectors count matching elements in document order. When repeating a block, its HTML and advertising tag must support multiple instances.
Install and enable the Pages application before creating or editing block placements. Existing rules will resume when Pages is available.
Pages is unavailable. Pages block sources require Pages to be installed and enabled. Administrators with permission to manage template code can still create and edit custom IPS template placements.

Leave empty for all three device classes. Detection uses the IPS platform and user-agent string, not screen width. Unrecognized devices use Desktop. Resizing does not change the class. An iPad using a desktop user agent may be detected as Desktop.

Insert before the target, inside at its start, inside at its end or after the target. A body target permits only the two inside positions; content cannot be inserted outside it. The position must be valid for the target’s HTML context.
New rules start disabled. Diagnostics can help you check the configuration before enabling the placement.
Place existing Pages blocks using a native template hook or a CSS selector. New and duplicated rules start disabled. Lower order values run first; the arrow controls change the global rule order.

Place an existing Pages block or custom IPS template code using a native template hook or a CSS selector. New and duplicated rules start disabled. Lower order values run first; the arrow controls change the global rule order.

Use a standard CSS selector, for example #forum-category_12 > .ipsData__item:nth-child(2). Prefer stable IDs and data attributes. A missing target leaves the block unplaced. The browser checks selector syntax.

The master switch controls every placement rule. Eligible pages bypass shared page caching so platform and group targeting remain correct. Purge any external CDN or reverse-proxy page cache after changing placements. Content and permissions are managed in Pages.
Lower values run first. Rules with the same order use their ID as a tie breaker.

Use HTML and native IPS template syntax, for example {expression="'Hello world'"}. This example displays Hello world without any extra extension. This code can execute PHP on the server with the application’s permissions; grant editing access only to trusted administrators. Raw PHP opening and closing tags are not accepted. The limit is 65,535 bytes. Pages block permissions do not apply to custom code: visibility is controlled by this rule’s member groups and by the code itself.
